author: Al Jazeera English
description:
How and why did Venezuela fall prey to the US special forces attack on Caracas on January 3, 2026, and what’s the political backstory?

Once a showcase US ally awash with oil money, Venezuela has descended into crisis and confrontation.

This film tracks the country’s arc from 1970s petro-democracy to the 1989 Caracazo riots, Hugo Chavez’s rise and radical reforms, the turbulent 2002 coup attempt against him, and the deep economic collapse and mass exodus under President Nicolas Maduro. Framed around the dramatic US special forces operation, with bombing raids on the capital and Maduro toppled from power, this one-off special asks how a country so rich fell so far. 

Through first-hand testimony, expert analysis and rare archive, it shows how the fate of many Latin American countries is still shaped by US power, as the whole continent braces itself for further intervention under the current US administration.

The US withdrawal from the World Health Organisation officially takes effect on 22 January, one year after President Donald Trump first announced the decision. 
Trump cited funding disparities and alleged Chinese influence over the WHO's handling of COVID-19, claims never substantiated. 
The WHO historically relied on US contributions of $160m to $800m annually, roughly 15 percent of its budget. 
China has pledged to increase its funding, and other member states approved a 20 percent rise in dues to offset the American shortfall.

Al Jazeera's Gabriel Elizondo reports from the United Nations in New York.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
There have been outbreaks of violence in Syria, despite a four-day ceasefire between the government and the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF).
Both sides accuse each other of carrying out attacks in the north of the country. 

Syrian security forces have sent large reinforcements to maintain security at the al-Hol camp in northeastern Syria. 
The Syrian government says members of the Kurdish-led SDF tasked with guarding the camp left without any coordination.
It's home to around 24,000 people, most of them women and children, who are linked to ISIL fighters. 
Al Jazeera has spoken to some of the residents.

They'd previously been held at a facility in Hasakah.
